paper.title: Hierarchical Prompting Assists Large Language Model on Web Navigation
paper.central_claim: A simple hierarchical prompting approach, ASH (Actor-Summarizer-Hierarchical): a dedicated Summarizer prompt first builds an action-aware, condensed observation, and an Actor prompt then predicts the next action from the summarised history; it outperforms the previous state-of-the-art prompting mechanism (ReAct) on WebShop task success (abstract: 6.2%; body: 6.8%, 29% relative), helps most on long trajectories, reduces invalid-action hallucination and mitigates the need for explicit reasoning, with potential for interactive decision making tasks with long observation traces in general.
paper.identity_note: The dispatch text called this the Mind2Web dataset paper; the pinned text is the ASH prompting paper (WebShop), which does not cite or use Mind2Web. Mind2Web (2306.06070) was not used as a nearest neighbour.

signatures.object: per-step raw web observation (WebShop text_rich page: search results, product pages) before it enters the agent context; baseline = ReAct raw observation
signatures.information: Summariser input: instruction, previous action a_{t-1}, raw page o_t, few-shot demonstrations with a step-by-step instruction; stateless (no earlier observations). No privileged labels or test data stated.
signatures.operation: LLM writes a short rationale then 'info[...]' condensed observation: remove instruction text, keep ~3 closest products, filter options, keep navigation buttons, add hints/'(to click)' tags
signatures.conditions: effect claimed when raw observation is long/irrelevant; GPT-3.5 4k window
signatures.feedback: none beyond the environment page after the previous action; invalid-action messages surface in the raw page and trigger hints
signatures.selection_rule_data: none: single greedy generation, no candidate selection, no verifier; relevance judgement is the LLM's own
signatures.persistence: o'_t replaces o_t in the Actor's history H'_t for the rest of the episode; nothing carried across tasks
signatures.later_use: later steps of the same episode read summaries only
signatures.failure_boundary: under-compression on very long pages and hallucinated option (anecdotes E.1/E.2), rates unmeasured

signatures.object: next-action prediction over the summarised history
signatures.information: instruction plus alternating condensed observations and actions; actions search/click/think; rules incl. 'Follow Hint in Observation carefully'
signatures.operation: few-shot prompted actor predicts one action per step
signatures.conditions: greedy decoding, 20-step cap, termination on consecutive invalid actions
signatures.claimed_effect: with DIRECT actor: 22.2 -> 27.4 SR (Figure 5b, medium confidence)
signatures.failure_boundary: repeated invalid actions still 10.4% of failures

retention_trace.reason: Static prompting harness; no claim that a change is selected and persisted for later tasks. Summaries live only within one episode (before -> summarise each page -> Actor history -> same episode); no selection data, no cross-task persistence, no improver gain claimed.

matches.reason: Operation is a two-stage split of per-step processing (condense observation, then act) with a text handoff; the authors present exactly this decoupling and separate prompt development (E044). It fits the main-card signature at the coarse level only. The sub-card C25 (singleton under this parent) requires a machine-checkable artifact and a sound solver closing the loop, which this method lacks, so sub_id is null.

rs_pattern.outside_taxonomy_considered: Also defensible: no RS card describes goal-conditioned LLM observation summarisation. Candidates opened and rejected: architectural_operator_substitution (needs proof the surrogate preserves a property; none), adapt_via_conditioning/C03 (few-shot is only the mechanism, the claim is not task-generalisation by conditioning), heterogeneous_decomposition/C04 (compression of trained artifacts with error decomposition).
rs_pattern.reason: Primary chosen at weak fit because the main-card operational signature (decompose -> route to separately prompted stage via an intermediate artifact) matches the authors' operation; the card's when-to-apply (a part better handled by a sound external/symbolic solver) does not hold. No supporting card is needed. No score depends on this label.

executes_pattern.reason: Executes the decomposition shape but not the verifiable-artifact / solver-feedback core.

resolves_problem.reason: Authors show gains but also residual summariser failures (E036, E037), SR 30.2% / 12.6%, a single environment; the long-observation problem is mitigated, not shown closed.

matches.operation_mapping: C13 prunes/restructures the text observation before the policy sees it. ASH's Summarizer does this with an LLM conditioned on goal and previous action (drop irrelevant products/options, keep navigation buttons) before the Actor sees it. Differences: C13 evidence is rule-based; the Summarizer is learned-by-prompting and also injects hints.

condition_checks.note: Success rate reported; refinement is LLM-based not rule-based; tokens per step not reported.
Raw vs summarised observation compared under the same backbone (ReAct vs ASH), but no other encodings (rule truncation).
Target loss/hallucination by the pruner occurs (E.1/E.2) and its recall is unmeasured; for F items 'unmet' means the failure mode is present or unaddressed.
Pruning cost unreported; single site, no per-category breakdown.

unassigned: Summariser-injected hints (information not in the raw page, e.g. 'No Search button found', '(to click)') are not covered by C13 prune/restructure.
Decoupled development of summariser and actor prompts as a design principle (no domain card).

considered_not_matched.C15: history compression keeps recent steps raw; ASH never keeps raw observations in history
considered_not_matched.C16: retained content is nominated by a stateless summariser per step, not by the agent for later steps
considered_not_matched.C20: ReAct-style think action is inherited, not the contribution

revision_proposals.proposal: Widen C13 wording to include goal-conditioned LLM summarisation of the text observation (with optional hint injection) as a variant distinct from rule-based pruning; add the summariser under-compression and hallucination as C13 failure modes.
revision_proposals.support: single paper (2305.14257); candidate only, do not apply in-batch

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: split per-step processing into a condense stage and an act stage joined by a text artifact. Domain: the condense stage is the observation-pruning operation of C13; the act stage is the ordinary prompted policy.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS requires a verifiable artifact and sound solver (absent); C13 evidence is rule-based and reports tokens/step (absent). Mapping holds at the operation level only.

claims.text: ASH outperforms ReAct on WebShop with code-davinci-002 (SR 23.4 -> 30.2, avg score 53.4 -> 56.7).
claims.setting: WebShop text_rich, full product space, 500 trajectories, greedy decoding, max 500 tokens, 20-step cap
claims.baseline_control: authors' re-implementation of ReAct, same base model/decoding
claims.selection_vs_test: no separate dev set stated; base model chosen on 50-task subset of the same 500 tasks (E027)
claims.result_denominator: 500 tasks (seeds 501-999 in code: 499 values); success=score 1.0; failures include invalid-action terminations and step-cap
counterevidence: E002 vs E003: abstract states 6.2 pt, body 6.8 pt
E025: baseline re-implemented, prompt not shown
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported single-run gain of 6.8 pt SR on WebShop vs their own ReAct; not shown to exceed noise or a rule-truncation baseline.

counterevidence: E008/E009: ReAct frequently exceeds the 4k context; the gap mixes relevance with token reduction
claims.allowed_conclusion: ASH avoids the context-overflow failure of raw-observation ReAct under a 4k window; the semantic value of summarising is not separated from simply shortening.

claims.text: ASH helps more on long-horizon tasks (>11 steps: ReAct 7.4 vs ASH 38.2 avg score).
claims.setting: Figure 4 bins by realised trajectory length
claims.selection_vs_test: post-hoc stratification of the same runs
claims.result_denominator: per-bin counts only in the figure (unreadable)
counterevidence: trajectory length is an outcome (looping/failing runs are long), so bins are not task-difficulty strata
claims.allowed_conclusion: ASH-run long trajectories score higher than ReAct-run long trajectories; not a difficulty-matched comparison.

claims.text: ASH reduces hallucination-style failures (repeated invalid actions: 12.7% -> 10.4% of failures, 18% relative).
claims.result_denominator: share of failures; failure counts differ between methods
claims.allowed_conclusion: Share of failures that are repeated invalid actions is lower by 2.3 pt; causal story untested.

claims.text: ASH mitigates the need for explicit reasoning: DIRECT+ASH (27.4) beats ReAct (23.4) 'by a significant margin'.
claims.result_denominator: 500 tasks; bar labels extracted from separate lines (medium confidence)
counterevidence: no significance test; ASH with ReAct-style actor (30.2) is still above DIRECT+ASH (27.4), so reasoning still helps
claims.allowed_conclusion: A 4-pt SR difference in one run; explicit reasoning is not shown to be unnecessary.

claims.text: (Framing) The approach has broad applicability to interactive decision making with long observation traces.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported beyond WebShop; stated by the authors as a limitation.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Interactive WebShop environment with programmatic reward; single simulated site, no unseen environment or cross-platform result, so not transfer (EVIDENCE.md rules 1-2). No learned verifier.
assessment.author_claim_kept: broad applicability to interactive decision making; ASH > ReAct; helps long trajectories; fewer hallucinated invalid actions; reduces need for explicit reasoning
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the authors' single greedy run on 500 WebShop text-rich tasks, replacing raw observations in a ReAct-style prompt with per-step LLM summaries raised reported success from 23.4% to 30.2% (code-davinci-002) and from 3.0% to 12.6% (gpt-3.5-turbo, where ReAct hits the 4k window), against the authors' own ReAct re-implementation.
cannot_say: gain exceeds run-to-run noise or a rule-truncation baseline
summarisation, not mere shortening, causes the gain
works outside WebShop or in real browsers
assessment.reproduction: none; all results are author_report, no code was run

G.reason: Specific, sourced bottleneck: long/noisy raw observations (WebShop pages) degrade a prompted agent (context overflow at 4k for gpt-3.5-turbo; ReAct avg score 7.4 beyond 11 steps; 12.7% of ReAct failures are repeated invalid actions). The authors' own lineage (ReAct as closest, action-structure work, multi-stage prompting) is explicit and the residue (observation encoding, unlike action/reasoning shaping) is correctly located. Not 4: nearest-neighbour comparison is a single authors' re-implementation of ReAct; ReAct/WebShop source text is not pinned in this material, so lineage rests on the authors' description; the hand-trimmed (top-3) observation setting of the original ReAct run is the most relevant adjacent practice and is mentioned only in a footnote; stakes outside one simulated shop are asserted, not shown; whether overflow or irrelevance is the bottleneck is not separated.

M.reason: The operation, information and assumptions are reconstructible: a stateless Summarizer sees instruction, previous action and raw page, writes a short rationale then 'info[...]' with relevant products/options retained, navigation buttons kept, hints added; the Actor sees only summarised history. This addresses the stated bottleneck (length and irrelevance) directly and plausibly (E032-E035, E040). Not 4: the mechanism hypothesis (noise triggers hallucination) is labelled a hypothesis and not tested; no distinguishable prediction versus the obvious cheap alternative (rule-based top-k truncation, history truncation) is stated; the summariser can also add information (hints), so gains cannot be attributed to pruning alone.

X.reason: Operation chain is fully disclosed and reconstructible: both Summarizer and Actor prompts (C.1-C.4) for both models, action space (search/click/think), step cap 20, invalid-action termination, greedy decoding, environment config and seeds (E019-E021, E041, E042, E032-E039). Failure modes are shown (under-compression on long pages, hallucinated option; E036, E037) and an error-recovery hook exists (hints on invalid action). Not 4: summariser fidelity (recall of the target among retained options, hallucination rate) is never measured; the ReAct baseline prompt is not shown; domain-card C13 conditions (tokens per step, per-category effects) and transfer boundaries are not addressed; no verifier gates a bad summary.

E.measurement.reason: Outcome comes from the WebShop environment's programmatic attribute-match reward (success = score 1.0), 500 tasks, two metrics, two base models, plus a 50-task subset on a third (E004-E007, E016, E028-E031); no learned judge. Not 4: the ReAct comparator is the authors' re-implementation with undisclosed prompt and no sanity check against the published ReAct number; the abstract's 6.2% contradicts the body's 6.8% (23.4->30.2); Table 2 rates imply n=52 not 50; per-length counts exist only as a figure; the 500 trajectories vs seeds 501-999 (499 values) is unreconciled.

E.causality.reason: Relevant controls exist: same base model and decoding for ASH vs ReAct, a second base model, and DIRECT vs DIRECT+ASH which removes the reasoning actor while adding the summariser (E004-E007, E014). Key gaps: (a) no ablation of summariser inputs or hints (previous action, step-by-step rationale, hint injection) nor of Actor-prompt additions (E038, E039) that ReAct may lack; (b) no cheap alternative such as top-k rule truncation or history truncation, although the authors' own footnote says the original ReAct setting trimmed results to top 3 (E017); (c) the gpt-3.5-turbo gain (3.0 -> 12.6) is explained by 4k context overflow (E008, E009) and so is confounded with relevance; (d) ASH uses at least two LLM calls per step versus one, unequal compute; (e) the 'hallucination' mechanism is a stated hypothesis (E013); (f) 'mitigates need for explicit reasoning' is only partly supported: ASH with ReAct-style actor (30.2) still beats DIRECT+ASH (27.4).

E.holdout.reason: All evidence is from one simulated e-commerce environment (WebShop, text-rich), one split, with no second environment, unseen sites or real browser; the authors concede no more realistic benchmark was tried (E022, E023) while the abstract claims broad applicability to interactive decision making. Selection/test separation is not stated: the base-model choice was made on a 50-task subset of the same 500 evaluation tasks (E027), and it is not stated whether few-shot demonstration instructions overlap the evaluation seeds (E041); contamination of code-davinci-002 with WebShop-like text is not discussed. The narrow claim (WebShop, two backbones) is addressed; the broad claim has no evidence.

E.statistics.reason: Single greedy run per configuration (E019); no seeds, variance, confidence interval or significance test, yet 'significant' is used (E014). By arithmetic only (our inference): at p~0.25-0.3 and n=500 the binomial SE of a success rate is ~2 pt, so a 6.8 pt gap is probably but not demonstrably outside noise, and the 4.0 pt DIRECT+ASH vs ReAct gap and 2.3 pt invalid-action share gap are not. Failure analysis is partial (invalid-action share, two anecdotal summariser failures) and per-length counts are unreadable in this extraction; Table 2 n is internally inconsistent (E031); 'trajectory length' bins are conditioned on outcome (failing/looping runs are long), which weakens the long-horizon reading.

E.cost.reason: Some budget parity at the interface level: same base model, greedy decoding, max 500 tokens, 20-step cap and termination rule for both methods (E019-E021). But ASH makes at least two LLM calls per step and carries a long few-shot Summarizer prompt (C.1/C.2), and no tokens, calls, latency or dollar cost is reported anywhere in the main text or appendices (keyword search for cost/token/latency/price found only the max-token setting); the only compute-related result is qualitative (context overflow of ReAct).
